tasks.short: Make public address announcements about the flight.

steps.what: Read the flight facts on the flight deck
Prepare the wording for these flight announcements
Make public address announcements regarding these flights

tasks.design: The airline pilot reads the flight number, destination, departure time and any delay on the flight deck {OTHER}, then prepares the wording in {DOCS}. The pilot speaks the public address announcement. No system speaks to passengers.
tasks.previous_blocker: The announcement is live speech. A wrong line cannot be taken back.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes that. The flight facts are already on the flight deck.
tasks.still_hard: Tone, delays and nervous passengers stay with the pilot who can hear the cabin.
tasks.human_edge: The pilot hears the cabin and can change tone when passengers are nervous.
tasks.altitude: The week is unchanged. The pilot still makes every announcement.

reach.task: Speak to passengers about the flight
reach.learn: Which flight facts belong in a public address announcement and which stay off it.

evidence.claim: The pilot speaks and passengers hear it live. A wrong line cannot be taken back. The source says model knowledge.
National aviation rules differ. This design does not replace the pilot as the person who makes the announcement. The source says model knowledge.

assumptions: Means prior sums to 100. Documents stay 4. The 0.7 remainder on screens and the 0.7 remainder on in-person talk take the two points, so screens are 1 and the talk is 95. Mail at 0.6 rounds to zero and is omitted. The zero workbook prior is omitted.
No new weekly chore, because nothing is built.

Flight-facts contract: flight number, destination, departure time, and delay when the flight deck shows one. Producer is the flight deck. Fallback: the pilot reads the same facts from the flight plan.
The wording note does not leave the aircraft and is not a record other people rely on after the flight. The spoken announcement is the act, so the note is not gated.
No system speaks on the public address.
unknowns: Whether this airline scripts standard lines the pilot must still say.
research_questions: Which delays must the pilot announce on the public address?

incremental.description: No new weekly chore. Nothing is built for the spoken announcement.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The announcement stays spoken by the pilot and no step is shortened.

tasks.short: Coordinate with ground crews and air traffic control, and brief the crew.

steps.what: Read the flight plan on the flight deck
Write the flight and test procedures for the crew
Coordinate flight activities with ground crews and air traffic control
Inform crew members of the flight and test procedures

tasks.design: The airline pilot reads the flight plan on the flight deck {OTHER} and commits the flight and test procedures in {DOCS} before the briefing. Radio with ground crews and air traffic control stays with the pilot, and the crew briefing stays a face-to-face talk. That talk is not a workflow: the judgement is in the moment, and a wrong instruction can harm people.
tasks.previous_blocker: A wrong instruction can harm people, and the judgement is in the moment.
tasks.enabler_now: The flight plan is already on the flight deck. That does not turn the radio into a workflow.
tasks.still_hard: A test procedure or a ground conflict can change in the minute it is spoken.
tasks.human_edge: The pilot hears a ground conflict or a test change in the minute it is spoken.
tasks.altitude: The week is unchanged. The pilot still coordinates by radio and still briefs the crew.

reach.learn: Which flight and test procedures the crew must hear before the aircraft moves.

evidence.claim: Radio with air traffic control and the crew briefing stay with the pilot, because a wrong instruction can harm people. The source says model knowledge.
National rules differ. This design does not replace the pilot's coordination with air traffic control. The source says model knowledge.

assumptions: The workbook prior of 0.3 and the mail prior of 3.7 are dropped. This coordination is radio and a face-to-face crew briefing. The remaining 96 scales to screens 3, procedures 15 and in-person talk 82.

The 82 in-person points are split 62 to radio and 20 to the crew briefing. That split is not a measured timing study. It only separates the outside radio from the talk with colleagues. Neither act is shortened.
Ground crews in the radio step are the handler outside this airline's flight crew, together with air traffic control.
Crew members are colleagues. The briefing is not a send outside the organisation.
The procedures text is a record the crew uses. The pilot commits it before the briefing. The briefing does not edit the committed text.
Flight-plan contract: route, departure, aircraft and the test items already on the plan. Producer is the flight deck. Fallback: the pilot reads the same plan in the flight planning system.
No new weekly chore, because nothing is built.
unknowns: Whether the ground crew on this ramp is this airline's own staff. If they are colleagues, the radio step would not be an outside act.
research_questions: Which flight and test procedures must be said to the crew before the aircraft moves?

incremental.description: No new weekly chore. Radio and the crew briefing stay as they are.

approvals.approved_version: flight and test procedures committed for the crew

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Neither the radio nor the crew briefing is shortened. The pilot commits the written procedures at the same time as today.

tasks.short: File the instrument flight plan and coordinate with other air traffic.

steps.what: Classify route notices in the flight planning system

loop.input: The route, the alternates, the time window, and the notices the flight planning system already lists.
loop.output: Each notice marked on this route or not, plus any notice left unclassified.
loop.check: A notice is marked off this route only when its place and time were compared with the route, the alternates and the time window. A notice the loop cannot classify stays for the pilot.
loop.stop: When a notice cannot be classified, the loop stops and the pilot reads the rest.
loop.why_not_simpler: Matching only airfield codes hides a notice that names a region or a route segment and not the code.

steps.what: Review the instrument flight plan text
File instrument flight plans with air traffic control on the flight planning system
Ensure these flights are coordinated with other air traffic

tasks.design: A bounded loop in the flight planning system {OTHER} marks notices whose place and time sit outside this route, the alternates and the time window. The airline pilot still reviews the instrument flight plan in {DOCS}, files that plan from the flight planning system {OTHER}, and then coordinates with other air traffic in person. The system already computes the route. That existing work is not a labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notices are free text, and filing commits the flight to other traffic.
tasks.enabler_now: The flight planning system already holds the route, the alternates, the time window and the notices.
tasks.still_hard: A notice that names a region rather than a code, and the decision to file, stay with the pilot. A flight planning failure can affect many passengers.
tasks.human_edge: The pilot decides whether an unclassified notice changes this flight.
tasks.altitude: The pilot still reviews and releases every instrument flight plan. Off-route notices take less reading when the loop can classify them.

reach.learn: Which notices change an instrument flight plan before it is filed.

evidence.claim: An AI module ranks NOTAMs. Live use is not stated.
Lido Flight 4D computes routes, profiles and fuel against weather and airspace restrictions, and digital NOTAMs.
NATS flight planning failure, 28 August 2023: over 700,000 passengers affected, 34 recommendations.
Annex III point 2 names digital infrastructure, road traffic and utilities, not aviation.
Only Art. 6(1), 102-109 and 112 apply, so requirements come through EASA rules.

assumptions: The 0.6 workbook prior is the fuel figure inside the flight plan, so it is absorbed into the plan text: 36.3. The 11.4 mail prior is the filing transmission, kept as its own flight-planning-system step, not a mailbox. Notice reading stays 8.9 and the talk stays 43.4.
Largest remainder gives notice reading 9, plan text 36, filing 11 and the talk 44. The tie between filing and the talk goes to the talk because its original quantity is larger.
The airline already uses a flight planning system. Existing route and fuel computation earns no labour saving. The source for that existing use is model knowledge.

The only shorter step is notice reading, remaining 70. That 70 is not a measured study. It is the reading that remains after notices whose place and time are clearly outside the route, the alternates and the time window. The pilot still reads on-route and unclassified notices, still reviews the plan, still files it and still talks to air traffic control.
Notice contract: route, alternates, time window, and each notice's place and time. Producer is the flight planning system. Fallback: the loop stops and the pilot reads every notice in the same step.
The plan review is not gated. The filed plan is the version that leaves, and the later talk does not edit it.
The pilot reviews and files. This task does not add a dispatcher.
No new weekly chore. The loop runs inside the flight planning system the pilot already opens. Its consent check reads notices and the route, not a score of the pilot.
The loop does not file the plan.
unknowns: Whether this airline's flight planning system already marks notices by route, or the pilot still pages through the full list.
research_questions: Which notice wordings does this airline's flight planning system already store as place and time?

already_counted.description: Reading notices that sit on this route or that the loop leaves unclassified.
Reading the instrument flight plan text before filing.

incremental.description: No new weekly chore. The loop runs inside the flight planning system the pilot already opens.

approvals.approved_version: instrument flight plan filed with air traffic control

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only off-route notice sorting is shorter. The pilot still reviews the plan, files it and talks to air traffic control. The low case is when most notices touch this route or cannot be classified.

tasks.short: Do minor maintenance, or arrange major maintenance.

steps.what: Perform minor maintenance on the aircraft
Open this aircraft in the technical log
Write the defect and the work into the technical log
Arrange major maintenance with maintenance control

tasks.design: The airline pilot still does the minor work on the aircraft. The technical log {OTHER} places the aircraft, the date and the flight it already stores, and the pilot writes the defect and the work and commits that entry. A separate message in {EMAIL} asks maintenance control to arrange major maintenance, and the pilot sends that message.
tasks.previous_blocker: The pilot has to see the defect and judge whether it is still minor.
tasks.enabler_now: The technical log already stores the aircraft, the date and the flight, and can place them. The pilot still writes the defect.
tasks.still_hard: A defect that looks minor can ground the aircraft. The request to maintenance control is still the pilot's words.
tasks.human_edge: The pilot sees the defect and judges whether it is still minor.
tasks.altitude: The pilot still does the minor work and still decides whether maintenance is minor or major.

reach.learn: Which defects the pilot still treats as minor and which go to maintenance control.

evidence.claim: AVIATAR Technical Logbook: prefilled text, input masks, offline sync, and a link to the maintenance system.
Logs that tie times and fuel to named pilots can check performance: consent under 27(k) and (l).
The pilot still does the minor work by hand. The source says model knowledge.

assumptions: The 1.1 workbook prior is dropped. A pilot does not keep a separate workbook for a defect. The remaining 98.9 scales to screens 5, the maintenance message 5, the log text 24 and the physical work 66.
The physical work stays at remaining 100. Opening the log stays at remaining 100 and is the step that produces the aircraft header.
Header contract: aircraft registration, date and flight number. Producer is the technical log already on the aircraft. Fallback: the pilot types those three fields, and this step is not shorter.
Remaining 80 on the log write is not a measured study. The shorter part is only those three fields the log already stores. The pilot still writes the defect and the work.
The maintenance request is its own message. It does not edit the committed log entry. Maintenance control is this airline's own staff, so the message stays inside the organisation.

The log entry records the defect and the work, not a score of the pilot. Dutch works-council consent for logs of times and fuel does not apply to this entry. National rules still vary where a named log is treated as a performance record, so a short consent check is in the build.
The prior that this task is a workflow does not fit the physical work. Only the header placement is configuration of the existing log.
No new weekly chore. The header placement is native configuration, not a new weekly task.
unknowns: Whether maintenance control is inside this airline or a contracted organisation. A contracted recipient would make the message a send outside the organisation.
Whether the technical log already stores aircraft registration, date and flight number for the open aircraft.
research_questions: Does the technical log already store aircraft registration, date and flight number for the open aircraft?

already_counted.description: Judging on the aircraft whether the defect is still minor.
Writing the defect and the work into the technical log.

incremental.description: No new weekly chore. Header placement is configuration of the log the pilot already opens.

approvals.approved_version: maintenance request sent to maintenance control

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only placing the aircraft, date and flight on the log entry is shorter. The pilot still does the minor work, writes the defect and writes the maintenance request. The low case is when those header fields are not already stored on the open aircraft.
